tour.overview:
Porto, which gave its name to Portugal and to port wine, is a city of granite churches, blue-and-white tiles and steep streets tumbling to the Douro. Its historic centre has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996. Across the river, in Vila Nova de Gaia, the port houses have aged their wines in cool cellars for centuries.

This private day explores Porto on foot with a licensed guide, with a vehicle for the steep sections, a cellar visit and a river cruise.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Porto
• Type: private tour with licensed guide; vehicle for transfers; shared river cruise
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; steep streets

WHAT YOU SEE
• São Bento station and the cathedral.
• Livraria Lello and the Clérigos Tower.
• Ribeira.
• The Dom Luís I bridge.
• A port cellar.
• The six bridges.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide plans the route downhill, uses the vehicle for the steepest climbs and books timed tickets for the bookshop.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors, wine lovers, couples and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For the vineyards, choose our Douro Valley wine tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Livraria Lello requires a timed ticket. Porto is hilly: wear comfortable shoes.

days.name: São Bento, the cathedral, Livraria Lello, Ribeira, the bridge, a port cellar and a river cruise
days.description:
What to expect: Porto's tiled churches, riverside and port wine, with a licensed guide, tickets, a tasting and a cruise.

Your guide meets you at your hotel at about 9:30. You begin at São Bento station, whose great hall is lined with some 20,000 azulejo tiles showing battles and scenes of rural life. You walk up to the cathedral, a fortress-like Romanesque church with a view over the rooftops, then to the Clérigos Tower and the Livraria Lello, a neo-Gothic bookshop of 1906 with a curving red staircase and stained-glass ceiling.

After lunch (not included) – perhaps a francesinha, Porto's famous layered sandwich – you walk down to the Ribeira, the riverside quarter of narrow houses painted in bright colours, and cross the upper deck of the Dom Luís I bridge, an iron arch built in 1886 by a disciple of Gustave Eiffel, with a breathtaking view.

In Vila Nova de Gaia, you visit a port lodge, where wine ages in oak barrels and great vats, and taste several styles of port. You end with a 50-minute cruise under the six bridges of Porto, before your vehicle takes you back to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:45 – São Bento station.
10:15 – Cathedral.
11:00 – Clérigos Tower and Livraria Lello.
12:30 – Lunch break.
14:00 – Ribeira.
14:45 – Dom Luís I bridge.
15:15 – Port cellar tour and tasting.
16:30 – Six-bridges cruise.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Clérigos Tower climb can be added.
• The Church of São Francisco, covered in gilded wood, can be added.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, vehicle for transfers, bookshop ticket, port tasting, cruise, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: tasting.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: Livraria Lello, the port cellar tasting and the cruise.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide suggests a francesinha or a seafood restaurant.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the bookshop and the boat; tastings are for adults.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Porto is steep; the vehicle and the funicular can help.

faq.question: Is the cruise private?
faq.answer: The standard cruise is shared; a private boat can be arranged.

faq.question: Is Livraria Lello crowded?
faq.answer: Yes, often; timed tickets reduce the wait.

faq.question: Can we add the Douro Valley?
Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with grip and layers.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October; June brings the São João festival.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not obligatory in Portugal, but rounding up or leaving 5 to 10 percent for a guide or driver you were happy with is appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
